question: Which file service protocol allows the files to appear locally mapped to the client and provides view, store, and update capabilities on a remote Linux-based storage repository that also serves as a distributed file system standard for NAS?
theory: NFS lets a remote directory tree hosted on a Linux/UNIX-based storage repository appear as if it were mounted locally on the client, giving transparent view/store/update access to those files - and because NFS is an open, IETF-standardized protocol rather than a proprietary one, it has become the de facto distributed file system standard underlying NAS deployments, unlike CIFS (Windows-centric), iSCSI (block-level), or FTP (simple file transfer, not a mounted filesystem). (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 10 - NFS Concepts)
